_README: Acknowledged drift for the per-subsystem security audits, checked by
frontend/scripts/check-audit-freshness.mjs (runs in `npm run check`).
An audit's `Audited commit` is the code state its claims were verified
against. When the content under that audit's `Code paths` moves away from
it, the check goes red. Two ways out, both legitimate:
1. Re-verify the audit -> bump `Audited commit` in the doc, add a change
log entry, and drop the audit's entry from this file.
2. Review the drift and conclude it cannot move a verdict -> record the
current object id of each `Code paths` entry in `reviewedTrees`, and
append a dated record to `acknowledgements` saying why.
What is NOT legitimate is recording an object id without reading the diff.
The record is the evidence that someone did.
`reviewedTrees` holds git object ids (a tree for a directory, a blob for a
file), not commit SHAs. Get them from the check itself: when it fails it
prints the current id of every path that moved, ready to paste.
Object ids rather than commit SHAs because this repo squash-merges: a commit
SHA written during a PR stops existing when the PR lands, which used to cost
a follow-up commit per acknowledgement. Squashing rewrites history, not
content, so an object id survives it, along with rebases, cherry-picks and
force pushes.
`acknowledgements` is an ordered list of `{ date, note }`, oldest first, and
it is what bounds route 2. Option 2 used to be unbounded: one note string
that only ever grew, so the honest way out stayed available forever and the
audit itself was never read again. Two caps now end that run and force
route 1, whichever comes first:
- 8 acknowledgements. Each one judges its own delta in isolation; the
union of eight of them is not something a ninth reviewer can hold in
their head, and it is the union that decides whether a verdict moved.
- 90 days from the OLDEST record. Drift acknowledged in spring is being
defended by a judgement nobody has revisited.
Both clocks reset the same way: re-verify the audit, bump `Audited commit`,
and delete the entry from this file.

acknowledgements.note: Ctrl+P handed from the webview to the app, read against section 1. No sentence of this audit names it; verdict stays PASS. One path moved and the whole diff is webview_defaults.rs: VK_P leaves the list of accelerators kept with the browser, because globalShortcuts.ts now binds Ctrl+P to printing the open message, and the doc comment and two tests follow. Nothing else in frontend/src-tauri/src changed -- lib.rs, tray.rs, update_preference.rs, the three updater commands, PendingUpdate, DownloadedUpdate and beta_endpoint_override are byte-identical to a2e6d43, generate_handler! exposes the same eight commands, and capabilities/, tauri.conf.json, updates.ts, AboutSettings.svelte and windows-signed-release.yml are untouched. lib.rs also moves one assertion on WEBVIEW_DISK_CACHE_BYTES out of a test into a const assertion beside the constant, which changes no value and no argument the webview is built with, and the webview_defaults.rs doc comment gains a blank line; both are clippy cleanups with no behaviour in them. The handler this edits is attached to the webview controller in setup and is unreachable from the renderer, so section 1's IPC surface is unchanged; the key it stops keeping is a browser accelerator, which no updater path reads.

A doc comment, and nothing else. Verified the way the claim demands rather than by reading the intent: every added and removed line under this path that is neither a `///` line nor blank comes back empty. The paragraph corrected is the one the acknowledgement above introduced -- it said the app now binds Ctrl+P and prints the open message, while printCurrentView calls window.print() and is documented as printing the current view on purpose, so the next reader deciding whether a key may be denied at the WebView2 level was reasoning from behaviour the app does not have. keeps_browser_handling, is_removed_context_menu_item, attach_accelerator_keys, attach_context_menu and their tests are byte-identical, and lib.rs, tray.rs, update_preference.rs, the updater commands and generate_handler! are untouched, as are capabilities/, tauri.conf.json, updates.ts, AboutSettings.svelte and windows-signed-release.yml. No updater path reads any of it. Verdict stays PASS.

Print leaves the WebView2 context menu, read against section 1; no sentence of this audit names the context menu, and the verdict stays PASS. One path moved and the whole diff is webview_defaults.rs. Filtered to lines that are neither comment nor blank, it is exactly two things: is_removed_context_menu_item gains "print" in its matches!, and the test that pins that list is renamed and moves "print" from the kept names to the removed ones. The rest is doc comments saying why: the app now prints only the open message (globalShortcuts.ts), so a context-menu Print would print the folder list or settings page the key refuses to. keeps_browser_handling, attach_accelerator_keys, attach_context_menu and install are byte-identical, and lib.rs, tray.rs, update_preference.rs, the updater commands and generate_handler! are untouched, as are capabilities/, tauri.conf.json, updates.ts, AboutSettings.svelte and windows-signed-release.yml. The handler is attached to the webview controller in setup and is unreachable from the renderer, so section 1's IPC surface is unchanged, and no updater path reads a context-menu entry.

The startup update check's hint is hidden from the accessibility tree, read against section 1; no sentence of this audit names it, and the verdict stays PASS. One path moved and the whole diff is AboutSettings.svelte: the hint paragraph under the checkbox gains aria-hidden="true" and a two-line comment saying why. The checkbox, its checked binding to updateStartupCheck, handleStartupCheckChange and setUpdateStartupCheck, the aria-describedby that still names the paragraph, the update channel select and the Check for updates button are byte-identical, as are frontend/src-tauri/src, capabilities/, tauri.conf.json, updates.ts and windows-signed-release.yml. Nothing the updater reads or writes moved: whether the startup check runs still comes from the registry value through the same two shell commands, and the change is to what a screen reader hears, not to what the control does.

[Pre-structure accumulation.] Everything below was recorded in the single free-text note field the ledger carried before acknowledgements became dated records, and it therefore runs several separate reviews together in one string. It is kept verbatim rather than split, because the per-review object ids and dates it would need were never recorded. It counts as one acknowledgement; the next one starts a fresh record. The commit this id records is the change the audit's own v1.2 revision describes, so the doc and the code were written against each other rather than the doc trailing the code. Recorded here rather than by bumping `Audited commit` because the SHA would name a pre-squash branch commit that stops existing on merge — the failure mode this ledger was built for. Diff read in full: the login flow gains a fourth fail-fast guard in OAuth2LoginService (granted scopes vs. the provider's required mail scopes, rejecting before persistence), OAuth2ClaimsExtractor gains requiredMailScopes(), and the Google and Microsoft extractors state theirs. The other four Code paths entries are untouched — verified as an empty diff for SecurityConfig.java, OAuth2CompletedStateTracker.java, ExternalProviderLoginService.java and resources/static, so PKCE, the state gate and the failure-redirect hygiene are byte-identical. Checked the three things that could have moved a verdict. (1) The check only ever rejects: it compares two sets and throws, it never adds a scope to a request, so the E-row claim that scopes are hardcoded in application.properties with no in-app escalation path still holds exactly. (2) It cannot resurrect a dead account — it runs before persistence and calls markRequiresReauthIfExists, the same direction as the refresh-token guard, so the flag is still cleared only by a login that is complete. (3) No token material reaches a log: the WARN line names the missing scope constants and a masked email, and the audit entry carries the same, so the log-hygiene claim in §2 is unchanged. Verdict stays PASS. 4d3f6d6 touches this path in comments only — verified by filtering the commit diff to lines that are neither comment nor blank, which comes back empty; the whole change is javadoc on OAuth2TokenService.exchangeRefreshToken. The old text claimed the method was used during the initial OAuth2 login flow, which no call site supports: ExternalProviderLoginService persists the refresh token and leaves the exchange to the first IMAP connection, by which point the account exists and the cached getAccessToken path applies. The method was deliberately kept rather than deleted, and precisely because of this boundary — it is the only route into doRefresh(accountId = null), so removing it would also make the accountId != null branch unreachable, and that branch is what invalidates the cached token and marks the account requires_reauth after a permanent refresh rejection, which the E row and the §2 log-hygiene claim both rest on. No executable line moves, so PKCE, the state gate, the granted-scope check added in v1.2, the failure-redirect hygiene and the masked-email logging are byte-identical. Whether to wire the method back up or collapse the nullable parameter is left as its own change with its own re-verification. Verdict stays PASS. Java caller gate batch: the only change under feature/auth is three javadoc lines adding the @callerless tag to OAuth2TokenService.exchangeRefreshToken, recording in machine-readable form the decision #299 already wrote out in prose — it is kept because deleting it would make the accountId != null guard in doRefresh unreachable, and that guard is what marks an account requires_reauth. No code line changed.

Comment-only change under this path. 578526c moves the @callerless waiver on OAuth2TokenService.exchangeRefreshToken out of javadoc into a line comment, because @callerless is not a javadoc tag and Error Prone rejected it with InvalidBlockTag. Verified line by line rather than by reading the intent: every added and removed line under this path is a comment line. What the waiver protects is untouched — exchangeRefreshToken still exists, and the accountId != null guard in doRefresh it keeps reachable, the guard that marks an account requires_reauth after a permanent rejection, is byte for byte the same. No token exchange, refresh path, scope, redirect URI, PKCE step or credential storage path moved. Verdict stays PASS.

One idiom change under this path. 7ec2793 rewrites both cache lookups in OAuth2TokenService.getAccessToken from "cached.isPresent() && cached.get().isFresh()" to tokenCache.get(accountId).filter(CachedToken::isFresh). Optional.filter evaluates the predicate only when a value is present, exactly as the && short-circuit did, and the cache is still read once per lookup, so the freshness decision, the double-check under the refresh lock and the fall-through to doRefresh all behave as before. No token is cached, logged or transmitted differently, and no scope, redirect URI or PKCE handling is in the diff. Verdict stays PASS.

Two paths, one change, and the second path is why this note is longer than its delta. In OAuth2TokenService.doRefresh, a permanent refresh rejection now publishes AccountRequiresReauthEvent after the updateRequiresReauth / updateLastError pair it already wrote, so a listener outside this feature can close the account's now-unreachable IMAP connections; the base constructor takes the publisher and the two subclasses pass it through. ExternalProviderLoginService.markRequiresReauthIfExists is the third writer of that flag and does the same, from TransactionCallbacks.runAfterCommit because it is @Transactional - the purge behind the event waits on the per-account connection lock, which must not be waited on with the single-writer SQLite transaction open, and before the commit the flag is not durable. Nothing about either token flow moves: the same permanent-vs-transient classification decides the branch, the refresh lock, the cache invalidate, the metric and the thrown MailOperationException are unchanged, the login path still writes exactly the credentials and account fields it did, and no scope, redirect URI, PKCE parameter, client secret or token value is read, logged or transmitted differently. The event is deliberately minimal for that reason - it carries the account id alone, so no token or address reaches a listener with no business holding either. Placement inside the existing try is checked by a mutation that moves it out: the flag is what makes the account unreachable, so an event published after a failed UPDATE would ask for live connections to be closed. Three mutations in total, each red on exactly the test that claims its rule, each verified to have reached the tests. Verdict stays PASS.

A count, not a token, moves. OAuth2TokenServiceRegistry.totalCachedTokens summed getCacheStats() per service, but every service holds the one TokenCache bean, so the diagnostic summary reported each cached token once per provider; the registry now takes the TokenCache and reads its size once, and the per-service getCacheStats/CacheStats, left without a caller, are removed. No token value, refresh path, cache key or invalidation changes, so no claim of this audit moves and the verdict stays PASS.

The exception-text change of API_SURFACE_AUDIT.md 1.9: a new MailFailureCause enum in the exception package classifies a caught exception into a stable cause code, and MailConnectionException / MailOperationException gained constructors that take the cause and pass the classification, not the text, as the message argument. Under this audit's paths only OAuth2TokenService.tokenRefreshFailure changes: the refresh failure passes the caught exception as the cause of its MailOperationException instead of appending its text. The token flow, what is sent to the provider, storage and the refresh-rejection handling are unchanged, so no claim of this audit moves.

The mail layer's own English sentences kept out of responses, recorded in API_SURFACE_AUDIT.md as v1.10. Under this audit's paths only the message keys of six throws change. OAuth2LoginService's three rejections (no e-mail, no stable user id, no refresh token) name error.mail.oauth2NoEmail, oauth2NoUserId and oauth2NoRefreshToken instead of passing their English sentence as the argument of error.mail.operationFailed; OAuth2TokenService's missing stored refresh token names error.mail.accountRequiresReauth, a token response without access_token error.mail.oauth2NoAccessToken and a permanent refresh rejection error.mail.oauth2AuthorizationRevoked, the last two with the provider's display name (Google, Microsoft) as their one argument. Error codes, statuses, the order of the guards, markRequiresReauthIfExists, the refresh lock, the cache invalidation, the requires_reauth marking, the metrics and the log and audit lines are unchanged, and no token, scope, redirect URI or PKCE parameter is read, logged or sent differently, so no claim of this audit moves. Verdict stays PASS.

Every not-found and validation error names a message key of its own, recorded in API_SURFACE_AUDIT.md as v1.11: ResourceNotFoundException(String) and ValidationException(String), which passed the message as the {0} of a generic key, are removed, and each site that used them names a key. Under this audit's paths only OAuth2CallbackController.success changes: its two rejections, a call outside a completed login flow and an authorized client missing from the store, name validation.oauth2.loginNotCompleted. The checks themselves, their order, the processLogin call, the removal of the in-memory authorized client and the redirect are unchanged, and no token, scope, redirect URI or PKCE parameter is read, logged or sent differently, so no claim of this audit moves. Verdict stays PASS. This is the eighth acknowledgement: the next change under these paths needs the audit re-verified.

Change under this path, read rather than waved through as a timing tweak. StartupTimingService swapped its reference clock: the anchor for processStartedAt and for every phase's startedAfterProcessMs moved from an Instant.now() taken in the class's own static initialiser to ManagementFactory.getRuntimeMXBean().getStartTime(), with a wall-clock constant recording how much boot had already passed when the class loaded. Section 1 is untouched by it: the diff does not enter StorageContextInitializer, reads or writes no crypto.bin, touches neither the VOXSEC1 format, the DPAPI USER-scope call, the buffer zeroing, the atomic private-permissioned write, nor the constant-time crypto.fingerprint comparison, and adds no path by which any of them could be reached earlier or skipped. The class holds no secret and opens no file. Section 2 holds: CryptoService is not in the diff, and the one place where boot timing and that section intersect - the self-test "warmed off the boot path" claim - is about when the self-test runs, which this change does not move; it only changes what a later dump reports about the time that had already elapsed. The new dependency is java.management, read-only and already in the sidecar's --add-modules list; it is an MXBean read, not a JNI or FFM call, so the "pure Java FFM (no JNI)" hygiene claim of section 1 is about a path this does not join. Section 3 residuals are unaffected - nothing about mail.db plaintext at rest or the same-user-malware exclusion turns on a clock source. The one observable effect outside the boundary is that startup-timings.json in the diagnostic dump now reports a start roughly four seconds earlier and correspondingly larger phase offsets: the same data category as before, no new field and no new value class, and the dump's privacy check is RELEASE_CHECKLIST section 7, which is flagged for a re-take on this candidate for exactly this reason.

A comment, and nothing else: the two changed lines of MailContentService are the comment on the catch around body extraction. It said the wrapped exception lets MailFacade surface a contentError on the cached body; the message detail no longer calls this service and the field is gone, so it now says the caller gets a typed mail error instead of a 500. The sanitize call, the cid collection, the plain-text escape, the byte cap and the oversize flag are byte-identical, and the body still reaches the frame only through /content, which returns what this service produced. Verdict stays PASS.

The exception-text change of API_SURFACE_AUDIT.md 1.9: a new MailFailureCause enum in the exception package classifies a caught exception into a stable cause code, and MailConnectionException / MailOperationException gained constructors that take the cause and pass the classification, not the text, as the message argument. Under this audit's paths only MailContentService changes, in one line: the failure to extract a message's text passes the caught exception as the cause of its MailOperationException instead of appending its text to the message. What the service extracts, sanitizes or renders is unchanged, so no claim of this audit moves.

Every not-found and validation error names a message key of its own, recorded in API_SURFACE_AUDIT.md as v1.11: ResourceNotFoundException(String) and ValidationException(String), which passed the message as the {0} of a generic key, are removed, and each site that used them names a key. Under this audit's path MailContentService changes in two throws: a message missing from the database names error.message.notFound, and one no longer on the server error.message.goneFromServer. What the service extracts, sanitizes, caps or renders is unchanged, so no claim of this audit moves. Verdict stays PASS.

Folder role detection by name matches whole names only. Two paths moved. dto: FolderRole.fromNameFallback compares the whole name, after lower-casing, removing diacritics, collapsing whitespace and dropping one INBOX./INBOX//[Gmail]//[Google Mail]/ prefix, against a list of English and Czech system folder names, instead of testing for substrings; 'bulk' moves from NEWSLETTERS to JUNK. core/diagnostic: only the javadoc of DiagnosticDumpService.folderLabels changes, to say the fallback now matches whole names; the rule it documents (every folder but INBOX is a pseudonym, A3) is unchanged. Checked against what the audit claims. (1) No endpoint, method, path, authentication rule, DTO field, validation constraint or error mapping moves: FolderRole is an enum the API returns as a folder's role, with the same constants. (2) What a response or the dump discloses does not grow: a folder can only lose a role it wrongly had, and the dump names it the same way either way. (3) Section 6's A3 text describes the fallback as a substring match; that was true at the anchor 55fdd1b and is recorded here as history, not rewritten. DiagnosticDumpPrivacyIT now checks both that a folder with a role word in its name stays USER on a real IMAP server and that a user folder named exactly 'Newsletters' is still a pseudonym. Verdict stays PASS.

Requests Spring MVC rejects before a controller runs get their own status. One path moved, exception/. GlobalExceptionHandler gains handleTypeMismatch (MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException -> 400 VALIDATION_ERROR with a violation naming the parameter; the value is not echoed) and handleRejectedRequest (405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED, 415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, 406 NOT_ACCEPTABLE, other ServletRequestBindingException -> 400 BAD_REQUEST), which sends the status and headers the exception carries as an ErrorResponse (Allow on 405, Accept on 415) and logs one WARN line; a 5xx binding failure (MissingPathVariableException) still goes to the catch-all. ErrorCode gains the three codes. Checked against the audit's claims. (1) No endpoint, path or authentication rule moves: these handlers run only for requests that already passed the security chain and failed in Spring MVC. (2) Error-response hygiene holds and narrows the catch-all's reach: every new message is a fixed bundle text with at most the HTTP method or the parameter name as argument, no exception text and no stack. (3) Section 7's note 'Framework-level request errors reach the catch-all' was true at the anchor 55fdd1b and is superseded by this change; the next re-verification rewrites it. FrameworkRequestRejectionTest covers each case through MockMvc and fails with 500 against the old handler. Verdict stays PASS.

Attachment part paths are validated and resolved the way IMAP numbers parts. Two paths moved. controller: MailReadController.downloadAttachment adds @Pattern(AttachmentService.PART_PATH_PATTERN) to partPath, positive part numbers joined by dots, next to the @NotBlank and @Size(max = 64) it had. AttachmentService validates the same pattern before the folder executor, and findPartByPath throws ResourceNotFoundException(error.attachment.partNotFound) for a path that leads nowhere instead of a MessagingException the executor misread as a missing folder, and returns a message's non-multipart body as its part 1, the path MimePartExtractor gives such an attachment, which could not be downloaded before. Checked against section 4's claims. (1) No traversal path opens: partPath is still only ever an index into jakarta.mail Multipart children, never a filesystem path, and the temp file is still created after findPartByPath with the stored stableId as prefix. (2) Section 4's 'the request then fails with the wrong status' and section 7's note on the attachment path were true at the anchor 55fdd1b and are superseded; a malformed path is now a 400 before any IMAP work and a missing part a 404 naming the attachment. (3) No endpoint, method or authentication rule moves. AttachmentServiceTest runs the download lambda on parsed MIME messages and MailReadControllerTest the 400s; against the old code they fail, and the single-part download errors with 'MIME part 1 was not found'. Verdict stays PASS.

The attachment lookup asks only a container for its content (IMAP/SMTP audit B1-12, recorded there as v1.18). One path moved, AttachmentService.java: findPartByPath calls getContent() only when isMimeType says multipart/* or message/rfc822, so a text part is no longer read whole into memory on the way to the copy. Read against section 4: the lookup still only indexes into Multipart children and never touches the filesystem, the temp-file name and the response headers are untouched, and the statuses section 7 and the #582 note describe (400 for a malformed path before any IMAP work, 404 naming the attachment for a missing part) are unchanged. Verdict stays PASS.

The exception-text change of API_SURFACE_AUDIT.md 1.9: a new MailFailureCause enum in the exception package classifies a caught exception into a stable cause code, and MailConnectionException / MailOperationException gained constructors that take the cause and pass the classification, not the text, as the message argument. Recorded in the audit itself as v1.9 (sections 3 and 7). Under this audit's paths: the exception package (MailFailureCause added, the two mail exceptions' constructors, GlobalExceptionHandler untouched), AttachmentService (the download failure and the temp-file race pass their exception as the cause, so the path stays in the log), and application.properties (health show-details=never). The claims about authentication, validation, attachment streaming and the diagnostic dump are unaffected; the verdict stays PASS.

The mail layer's own English sentences kept out of responses, recorded in the audit itself as v1.10 (section 3). One path moves, exception/: MailConnectionException(String) and MailOperationException(ErrorCode, String, HttpStatus), which passed the message as the {0} of error.mail.connectionFailed / operationFailed, are removed, and MailOperationException(ErrorCode, String) now passes MailFailureCause.UNEXPECTED there and keeps its message for the log. The cause-taking and key-taking constructors, MailFailureCause and GlobalExceptionHandler are unchanged. Every former caller either names a key of its own or is a guard on the app's own state, which now reads as unexpected. Read against section 3, which the same change updates; authentication, validation, attachment streaming and the diagnostic dump are not touched. Verdict stays PASS.

Every not-found and validation error names a message key of its own, recorded in API_SURFACE_AUDIT.md as v1.11: ResourceNotFoundException(String) and ValidationException(String), which passed the message as the {0} of a generic key, are removed, and each site that used them names a key. Recorded in the audit itself as v1.11 (section 3). Under this audit's paths: exception/ (the two constructors removed, javadoc on the remaining ones), feature/mail/controller (DraftController's page-size check names validation.pageSizeTooLarge with the limit and the requested size, as MailReadController and ContactController already did; ThreadingInternalController's missing account names error.account.notFound), and AttachmentService (a missing message names error.message.notFound, one gone from the server error.message.goneFromServer). Statuses, error codes, the validation itself, attachment streaming and the diagnostic dump are unchanged. Verdict stays PASS.

The second fix for B1-8, recorded in the audit itself as v1.25 (section 4h), and finding B1-14 (section 4n), which it turned up. Two files under feature/mail/service change. BoundedImapProtocol overrides writeCommand to start a new CommandBudget there, and readResponse charges every response until the next command, tagged or not, except an untagged FETCH while readingOneAtATime is set; the per-response bounds, the budget values and the refusal are unchanged, and the javadoc on the budget and the flag says what is now charged. ImapCondstoreCommands.readEach hands an untagged FETCH to its caller and to no response handler, still notifies every other response, and past its limit clears readingOneAtATime so the responses it drops are charged; the write, the BYE handling, handleResult and the failure past the limit are unchanged. No other file under the path changes. Re-read against sections 4h, 4m and 4n, which the same change updates; the verdict stays open findings.

The fix for B1-13, recorded in the audit itself as v1.26 (section 4m). One file under feature/mail/service changes: BoundedImapProtocol gains MAX_SELECTION_EXPUNGE_STEPS (1,000 x MAX_MESSAGES), a SelectionBudget field started afresh in writeCommand for a SELECT or EXAMINE, and a charge in readResponse after the per-response refusal: SelectionBudget records the largest EXISTS and charges each EXPUNGE, and each UID of a live VANISHED (liveVanishedUids, zero for the EARLIER form), that count plus the entries already expunged, refusing past the cap with the existing ImplausibleResponseException. The class javadoc and the field comment name the new budget. The command budget, the per-response bounds, the nesting check and the streamed FETCH handling are unchanged, and no other file under the path changes. Re-read against section 4m, which the same change updates; the verdict stays open findings.

The second fix for B1-10, recorded in the audit itself as v1.27 (section 4j), with section 4n widened by reading alone. One file under feature/mail/service changes: BoundedImapProtocol.NestingCheckedResponse.nestsDeeperThan, at depth 1, skips from a BODY[ in any case (opensBodySection, BODY_SECTION) to the next ] or the end of the response (sectionEnd), as Angus 2.0.5 reads a BODY section with readString; the quoted-string and literal skipping, the bound and everything else in the class are unchanged, and no other file under the path changes. Re-read against sections 4j and 4n, which the same change updates; the verdict stays open findings.

The mail layer's own English sentences kept out of responses, recorded in API_SURFACE_AUDIT.md as v1.10. Five files under feature/mail/service change, in the text a throw carries and nowhere else. The OAuth-without-TLS guards in ImapConnectionManager, MailConnectionProbe (IMAP) and SmtpTransportFactory (SMTP) name error.mail.oauth2RequiresTls with the protocol as argument; each still throws before any socket opens, with the same audit line, error code and status. ImapFolderService.findFolderNameByRoleOrThrow names error.mail.folderRoleNotFound with the role's display name as a message-source-resolvable argument (mail.folderRole.<ROLE>), same code and status. ImapAppendService changes only a comment and its import: the oversized-draft refusal still stops at the first byte past MAX_DRAFT_BYTES, and the send pipeline reports it by its MailFailureCause as before. No read, bound, budget or protocol handling moves, so no claim of this audit moves; the verdict stays open findings.

Every not-found and validation error names a message key of its own, recorded in API_SURFACE_AUDIT.md as v1.11: ResourceNotFoundException(String) and ValidationException(String), which passed the message as the {0} of a generic key, are removed, and each site that used them names a key. Under feature/mail/service four files change, in the key a throw names and nowhere else: MailFacade (a missing message, draft or conversation, and a move target missing from the folder list), AttachmentService and MailContentService (a missing message, and one no longer on the server), and ImapFolderExecutor (a folder the server reports missing, error.folder.notFoundOnServer). Which condition throws, when, and with which status and code is unchanged, and no read, bound, budget or protocol handling moves, so no claim of this audit moves; the verdict stays open findings.
